17D.6 Do not glory or trust in your riches.

precepts.text: The wicked call their lands after their own names, as Cain named the city after Enoch.
precepts.point: Cain called the city after the name of his son, as the wicked call their lands after their own names.

note.label: Genesis 4: Cain, Abel, and the Sons of the Wicked

precepts.why:
“Their inward thought is, that their houses shall continue for ever, and their dwelling places to all generations; they call their lands after their own names.” That is the way of the wicked, and Cain did just that: he builded a city “and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.”

In those days the lands were named after men, which is why the land Cain went out to was called Nod. And Cain found his wife there, and built a city there. You do not build a city for three people. There were already people on the earth in the time of Adam; the land of Nod, the wife, and the city are all proof that the earth was peopled.

precepts.text: Their inward thought is that their houses shall continue forever, and they call their lands after their own name.
precepts.point: Their bulls gender and fail not, their cow calveth and casteth not her calf. They are even prosperous in their animals.

note.label: Job 21: Why the Wicked Prosper

precepts.why:
“Their inward thought is, that their houses shall continue for ever, and their dwelling places to all generations; they call their lands after their own names.” That is the mind of the wicked in Job 21: “Their seed is established in their sight with them, and their offspring before their eyes. Their houses are safe from fear, neither is the rod of God upon them.” This is why they think the way they do, because no rod falls on them, so they think their houses continue forever and call their lands after their own name.

This is going twofold, dealing with the wicked of Israel and the wicked of Esau. This passage is the pride of Esau.

precepts.text: Nevertheless man being in honor abideth not, so the honor does not last.
precepts.point: Their bulls gender and fail not, their cow calveth and casteth not her calf. They are even prosperous in their animals.

note.label: Job 21: Why the Wicked Prosper

precepts.why: “Nevertheless man being in honour abideth not: he is like the beasts that perish.” The honor does not last. Their seed is established in their sight, their houses are safe from fear, and no rod of God is upon them, so they think the way they do. Nevertheless, man in honor abideth not. This is the pride of Esau, and it goes twofold, for the wicked of Israel and the wicked of Esau; neither one's honor abides.

precepts.text: Charge them that are rich not to be high-minded nor trust in uncertain riches but in the living God who giveth us richly all things to enjoy.
precepts.point: Riches are uncertain; money in an online bank cannot be reached when Wi-Fi and electricity go out, and then the rich man is in the same boat as the poor.

note.label: Psalm 49: The Vanity of Riches Against the Grave

precepts.why:
Paul gives the charge: “Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy”. That is the answer to the ones in Psalm 49 who “trust in their wealth, and boast themselves in the multitude of their riches”. Riches are uncertain. Money sitting in an online bank cannot be reached when the Wi-Fi and the electricity go out, and then the rich man is in the same boat as the poor man.

Many of Israel's own brothers and sisters trust in their riches. The charge to them is the same: be not high-minded, do not trust in uncertain riches, trust in the living God, the one who gives us richly all things to enjoy.

precepts.text: Riches profit not in the day of wrath, but righteousness delivereth from death.
precepts.point: Riches are uncertain; money in an online bank cannot be reached when Wi-Fi and electricity go out, and then the rich man is in the same boat as the poor.

note.label: Psalm 49: The Vanity of Riches Against the Grave

precepts.why:
“Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.” None of them “can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to God a ransom for him”. Celebrities and rich people watch their family members die and can do nothing about it. All the money for transplants, surgery and chemotherapy cannot save them from the grave if the Most High wants to take them.

What delivers from death is not riches but righteousness. That is why David has no cause to fear in the days of evil: the redemption of the soul is precious, and money does not buy it.

precepts.text: Neither their silver nor their gold shall deliver them in the day of the Most High's wrath, for the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy.
precepts.point: Riches are uncertain; money in an online bank cannot be reached when Wi-Fi and electricity go out, and then the rich man is in the same boat as the poor.

note.label: Psalm 49: The Vanity of Riches Against the Grave

precepts.why:
Zephaniah says the same of the day of the Lord: “Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the Lord’s wrath; but the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy”. He will “make even a speedy riddance of all them that dwell in the land.” Those who boast in the multitude of their riches will find their silver and gold cannot ransom them when the wrath comes.

Riches profit not in the day of wrath, and they cannot redeem a brother from the grave. Trust in uncertain riches fails at both ends; the living God is the only sure trust.

precepts.text: The devil told Christ all this power and glory is delivered unto him to give to whomsoever he will, so the wicked prospering without keeping the commandments shows whom they worship.
precepts.point: Man being in honor abides not; he is like the beasts that perish, boasting himself and naming things after himself but destined to die.

note.label: Psalm 49: The Vanity of Riches Against the Grave

precepts.why:
The devil told Christ, “All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” The power and glory of this world are delivered to the devil, and he gives them to whom he will. So when the wicked prosper without keeping the commandments, it shows who they worship.

That is who is behind the ones whose inward thought is that “their houses shall continue for ever”, who “call their lands after their own names”. The so-called white man names America after Amerigo Vespucci and names boulevards after dead men, thinking it will always be here for his children. But the Most High will take it from them, and everything returns to its natural name. Man being in honour abideth not; he is like the beasts that perish.

note.label: Psalm 49: The Vanity of Riches Against the Grave

precepts.why:
“Behold, these are the ungodly, who prosper in the world; they increase in riches.” The ones prospering and increasing in riches are the ungodly, the same ones in Psalm 49 who leave their wealth to others and call their lands after their own names. Their prosperity is not the blessing of the Most High; it comes from the one who said the power and glory of the world were delivered unto him.

Wise men die, and the fool and the brutish person perish, and leave their wealth to others. A rich man dying without a will leaves Esau to take his money and pay his own people with it. The ungodly boast themselves and name things after themselves, but they are destined to die like the beasts.
